facts.statement: The only known species, B. mansillai, was named after Juan Eduardo Mansilla, a museum technician who discovered the fossil.
facts.quote: The type and only known species is B. mansillai, with the specific name honoring the discoverer Juan Eduardo Mansilla, a museum technician at the Geology and Paleontology Museum of the National University of Comahue.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, MUCPv-1460, consists of a mostly complete right dentary found in the upper Portezuelo Formation.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen, MUCPv-1460, is a mostly complete right dentary that was found in rocks of the upper Portezuelo Formation.

facts.statement: The dentary bone is squared-off rather than curved, with teeth crowded at the front of the jaw.
facts.quote: The dentary is squared-off instead of curved when viewed from above or below, with the teeth crowded into the front of the jaw

facts.statement: Baalsaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous in Neuquén Province, Patagonia, Argentina.
facts.quote: from the Late Cretaceous of Neuquén Province, Patagonia, Argentina

facts.statement: Baalsaurus lived between 93.9 and 85.7 million years ago, during the Turonian to Coniacian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Turonian to Coniacian (93.9 to 85.7 million years ago)

facts.statement: Baalsaurus belongs to the parent group Titanosauria.
Baalsaurus is classified within the class Saurischia.
The genus was described by Calvo and González Riga in 2018.
The species name of the genus is mansillai.
